names.name: The Common White Saxifrage
names.note: Small reddish bulbils (kernels) at the root: white meadow saxifrage.

cul:275-the-common-white-saxifrage.ref: Culpeper, Complete Herbal: The Common White Saxifrage
cul:275-the-common-white-saxifrage.text: It is very effectual to cleanse the reins and bladder, and to dissolve the stone engendered in them, and to expel it and the gravel by urine; to help the stranguary; for which purpose the decoction of the herb or roots in white wine, is most usual, or the powder of the small kernelly root, which is called the seed, taken in white wine, or in the same decoction made with white wine, is most usual. The distilled water of the whole herb, root and flowers, is most familiar to be taken. It provokes also women’s courses, and frees and cleanses the stomach and lungs from thick and tough phlegm that trouble them. There are not many better medicines to break the stone than this.
